doc.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Studio work, Juggernaut in 1976, and joining Stan Kenton at nineteen
summary: Capp says he was hidden by studio work until starting Juggernaut with Nat Pierce in 1976; born in Worcester, he joined Kenton at 19 as his first pro job.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well actually, I’ve kind of been, over the last many years I’ve been kind of hidden as it were, by studio work. But back in 1976 I decided that I had enough of that, you know I mean not that I still don’t do an occasional studio call, but that was my main focus after I got off the road with the bands, the many bands I played with and acts and all of that, I settled in at the studios. And I made a good living doing that. And never gave up, ever gave up playing jazz. But unfortunately studio musicians don’t get any exposure into the jazz public. And so it wasn’t until ‘76 when I started Juggernaut with Nat Pierce, that I kind of threw the towel in on the studio stuff. And so it didn’t happen overnight. You know I’ve been around a long time as my age will attest.
You are East Coast — moved to the West Coast.
Right. I was born in Worcester, Massachusetts and I joined Stan Kenton when I was nineteen.
That was my first professional job.
That’s a kind of a high pressure job for a first one, too.
